purpose: Make one observed source page durable on the Sender before its cursor advances: partition it into numbered, byte-stable Ingest Batch fragments, seal each with the installation key, and commit them to the Sender Outbox with the cycle's next page position, counts, chain, and cursor in one SQLite transaction, or commit nothing. Version 2 adds two things. A change read that finds nothing, after the record type's catch-up Change Cycle has finished, can advance the change origin to its next token without staging a message. And the Outbox backlog can be read without loading any sealed message.

inputs.name: observed_page
inputs.description: One page from read-snapshot-page or read-change-page: record type, cycle identity, projection schema version, one-based page index, the position or changes token it was read from, its ordered projections or retractions, and its tentative next position or token with exhaustion or continuation state. A quiet change read is the first page of an unstaged Change Cycle identity, with no items and no further page.

inputs.name: staging_context
inputs.description: The Sender's active Sender Installation, its installation key alias, and the capability generation to stage under: its number, record and byte limits, and supported projection schemas.

inputs.name: installation_cipher
inputs.description: The 3ug InstallationCipher seam, which seals each fragment with AES-256-GCM under the non-exportable installation key.

inputs.name: sender_storage
inputs.description: The Sender's SQLite database: the record type's current snapshot attempt, the cycle's page-chain progress, and the Sender Outbox, read before sealing and again inside the commit transaction. Version 2 also reads and writes the record type's quiet change-origin advance, and answers backlog reads from the Outbox's health-data-free columns.

outputs.name: page_staged
outputs.description: Every fragment of the page sealed as an Ingest Batch Outbox Message under consecutive sequences, committed with the cycle's next page position, fragment and record counts, chain value, cursor, and finished state.

outputs.name: refusal
outputs.description: A named reason the page does not continue its cycle or cannot be staged under the generation, with nothing written.

outputs.name: block
outputs.description: One projection or retraction cannot fit in an otherwise empty fragment under the generation's limits, so the page is refused whole with nothing written or sealed.

outputs.name: conflict
outputs.description: The cycle, its snapshot attempt, or the Outbox sequence changed while the page was being sealed, so nothing was written and the page can be staged again from the new state.

outputs.name: cipher_failure
outputs.description: The installation key was missing, unusable, or unavailable, or the cipher failed unexpectedly, with nothing written.

outputs.name: storage_failure
outputs.description: A database read or the commit failed and rolled back, so nothing was staged.

outputs.name: change_origin_advanced
outputs.description: A quiet change read's next changes token and unread-since instant committed as the record type's change origin under its current snapshot attempt, with no Outbox Message, sequence, or cycle progress written.

outputs.name: outbox_backlog
outputs.description: One Sender Installation's queued Outbox Message count and total plaintext byte length, or whether one of its sequences is still queued, read without loading any sealed message.

observable_effects.name: installation-key-seal
observable_effects.description: Seals each fragment once through the installation cipher with authenticated data binding it to its Sender Installation and sequence; never creates, deletes, or opens with the key.

observable_effects.name: sender-storage-write
observable_effects.description: Applies this unit's Sender schema migrations, and commits either a page's Outbox Messages, the installation's sequence high-water mark, and the cycle's progress, or one quiet change-origin advance, each in one SQLite transaction or not at all.

owns: the Sender Outbox table, the per-installation sequence high-water mark, and the sealing and authenticated-data format of every Outbox Message, which later stagers append through and send-outbox-message opens
partitioning and sealing one observed page into Ingest Batch Outbox Messages through ingest-protocol's partition rule
each cycle's page-chain progress after its empty initial state: pages staged, fragment and record counts, chain value, saved position or changes token, unread-since instant, and finished state
the rule that a page continues its cycle from the saved position, and that a Change Cycle continues the record type's change stream from its current snapshot attempt's pre-read token
classification of cipher and storage failures into the named failures
the rule that a quiet change read may advance the change origin only after a Change Cycle under the current snapshot attempt has finished, so the catch-up cycle after every snapshot is always staged
health-data-free Outbox backlog reads, which later units use instead of loading sealed messages
does_not_own: reading pages, which belongs to read-snapshot-page and read-change-page
beginning snapshots and the current-attempt rule, which belong to begin-initial-snapshot and begin-reconciliation-snapshot
deciding when to stage, retry, or begin a Change Cycle, minting Change Cycle identities, and recording or reporting a per-type block, which belong to coordinate-sender-sync
Snapshot Completion and Change Completion messages, which belong to stage-sync-completion
Sync Checkpoints, which belong to stage-sync-checkpoint
adopting capability generations and the installation key's lifecycle, which belong to manage-sender-enrollment
delivery and receipt-bound removal of Outbox Messages, which belong to send-outbox-message
the Wire Protocol encoding, fragment chain, and partition rule, which belong to ingest-protocol
the Expo bridge between Kotlin and TypeScript
deciding whether to advance a quiet change read or stage it, which belongs to coordinate-sender-sync
